sum: A week from Pokhara through Gurung villages and the Modi Khola gorge to the lodges at 4,130 m inside the Annapurna Sanctuary, returning by the Jhinu hot springs.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide earns the fee above Deurali, by judging whether the avalanche section is safe to cross that morning and by holding beds in the small gorge lodges.

access: Pokhara is the base. Most trekkers take a jeep or the local bus to Ghandruk by way of Nayapul and Kimche, and finish at the jeep track across the suspension bridge from Jhinu Danda. Both drives take about three hours and are rough beyond Nayapul.

photo.a: The snow-covered south face of Annapurna I fills the skyline above Annapurna Base Camp, where two stone huts sit half buried in deep snow under a dark blue sky.
photo.c: The south face of Annapurna I from Annapurna Base Camp

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or jeep between Pokhara and the trailhead; the Kathmandu–Pokhara bus and city hotel nights in some packages only

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, and shared jeeps between Pokhara and the trail
tips: Carry all the cash you need from Pokhara; there is no cash machine on the route.
Reserve lodges from Bamboo upward in peak season. Each stop has only a handful of buildings.
No meat is served above Sinuwa. Expect dal bhat, noodles, eggs and potatoes.
Plastic water bottles are banned above Chhomrong. Carry a bottle and refill it at the safe-water stations or treat stream water.
Bring microspikes from December to March, when the trail above Himalaya can be icy.

days.note: About three hours by jeep through Nayapul and Kimche to the stand below the village, then a 20-minute climb on stone steps. Spend the afternoon in the old upper village and the Gurung museum.

Up for an hour to Komrong Danda, steeply down about 450 m to the Kimrong Khola, then a long traverse and climb to Chhomrong. A short day on the map that feels like a full one. Permits are checked on arrival.

n: Chomrong Mountain View Lodge and Restaurant
Excellent View Top Lodge and Restaurant

days.note: Down several hundred stone steps to the Chhomrong Khola bridge and up again to Sinuwa, then rolling forest trail to Bamboo and another hour to Dovan. Remember those steps: on the way back you climb them at the end of a long day.

A short day on purpose. The trail climbs through the last of the forest past Himalaya and the overhanging rock of Hinku Cave to Deurali. Stopping here keeps the height gain modest and puts you at the start of the avalanche section first thing tomorrow.

Leave at first light to pass the avalanche gullies before the sun loosens the slopes above. At Machhapuchhre Base Camp the valley turns west and opens, and a steady two-hour climb leads to base camp. This is a 900 m gain in sleeping height, so stop at MBC if you feel unwell.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 900 m in one day, well over the 500 m guideline. Split the climb if you can.

days.note: Stay out for sunrise on the south face, then start down after breakfast and cross the avalanche section before mid-morning. It is a descent of more than 1,800 m, and the wet stone steps in the forest are slippery.
Back through the forest to Sinuwa, down to the Chhomrong Khola and up the long staircase into Chhomrong, then a steep drop to Jhinu. The hot springs are by the river, twenty minutes below the lodges.

Cross the long suspension bridge to the jeep stand, about half an hour on foot, then drive down the Modi Khola to Nayapul and Pokhara. In the monsoon the track is sometimes blocked and you walk on to the next roadhead.
